title: Nonconvex first-order stationarity with biased gradients and approximate Hessians: no function-value channel
summary: Find an approximate first-order stationary point of the full objective, namely $\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g$. The interaction interface and admissible outputs are specified under ORACLE and OUTPUT, respectively.

description_paragraphs: Find an approximate first-order stationary point of the full objective, namely $\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g$. The interaction interface and admissible outputs are specified under ORACLE and OUTPUT, respectively.
The objective $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is $C^2$ and bounded below; nonconvexity is allowed.
The objective has a finite infimum, and the public initial point $x_0$ satisfies $f(x_0)-\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)\le\Delta$.
The gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le\beta\|x-y\|_2$.

Admissible parameter domain:

$$d\ge1,\ \beta,M_2,\Delta,\eta_1,\eta_2,\varepsilon_g>0$$

description_paragraphs: A query at $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns a vector $g(x)$ and symmetric matrix $H(x)$ satisfying
$$\|g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\eta_1,\qquad\|H(x)-\nabla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_2.$$
Replies may depend on the history, and performance must be guaranteed for every admissible reply rule. No function value or separate value-query channel is available.

The public inputs are $x_0$, the target accuracy, and $d$, $\varepsilon_g$, $\beta$, $M_2$, $\Delta$, $\eta_1$, $\eta_2$. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.
Return $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$.
The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.
The base error is
$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2.$$
The criterion uses the gradient norm itself. Squared norms, expectations, and probability guarantees are recorded separately and are not substituted automatically.

The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.
Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.
Arbitrary measurable adaptive algorithms with private randomness are allowed.
No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Expectation or probability is evaluated after fixing the instance; randomness comes from the algorithm's private random seed.

proofs.title: Indistinguishability without a function-value channel
proofs.statement: Biased derivative feedback cannot uniformly attain a gradient tolerance below the bias when two compatible objectives produce identical complete transcripts.
proofs.body:
Take $d=1$, $x_0=0$, and $f_\pm(x)=\beta x^2/2\pm\eta_1x$. Both objectives can legally return $g(x)=\beta x$ and $H(x)=\beta$. Gradient error is $\eta_1$ and Hessian error is zero. Their initial gaps are $\eta_1^2/(2\beta)$, so require this to be at most $\Delta$.

For $\varepsilon_g<\eta_1$, the true-gradient success intervals have centers $\mp\eta_1/\beta$ and radius $\varepsilon_g/\beta$, and are disjoint. Every finite or infinite derivative transcript is identical on the two instances, so the output distribution is identical. Their success probabilities sum to at most one, precluding a 2/3 per-instance guarantee. Independent positive quadratic coordinates embed the construction in higher dimension.

Exact function values distinguish these instances, so this impossibility does not transfer to an interface including a noiseless value channel. It is also not a classification of noisy-value interfaces.
proofs.scope: Biased gradients with no function values, exact or sufficiently accurate Hessians, and the stated initial-gap compatibility. Applies to arbitrary randomization because the transcripts coincide.
proofs.limitations: The mapped bound retains its complete model, oracle, algorithm view, guarantee, quantity, resource projection, and parameter-region conditions. This argument does not enlarge that scope.
